descriptions.semantic: The computational hardness assumptions a system's security reduces to (e.g. discrete-log, decisional/​computational Diffie-Hellman, q-strong-DH, knowledge-of-exponent in the algebraic group model, random-oracle behaviour of the chosen hash) hold against probabilistic polynomial-time adversaries at the deployed security parameter; and for proof systems with a structured reference string, the setup was generated honestly — at least one ceremony participant was honest and destroyed their secret ('toxic waste'), or the system uses a transparent (setup-free) construction.
descriptions.system_theoretic: Not a behavioural property of the implementation but an ENVIRONMENTAL/cryptographic assumption discharged into other properties (BPO:0003 ZK, BPO:0070 soundness, BPO:0073 leakage, signature validity). It is the boundary at which mechanical verification stops and cryptanalysis / ceremony auditing takes over.
descriptions.security: If an assumption fails — a hardness break (e.g. cryptographically relevant quantum computing for DLOG-based systems), retained toxic waste, under-parameterized security level, or a flawed ceremony — every property reduced to it becomes void simultaneously. This is a systemic single-assumption failure mode and must be tracked explicitly, not buried.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Concretely: curve/field choice and bit-security; hash choice and domain separation for Fiat-Shamir; CRS provenance and ceremony transcript verification; migration posture toward post-quantum or transparent constructions.
descriptions.formal_verification: Cannot be 'verified' by program-analysis tools. It is justified by published cryptanalysis, parameter selection to a target security level, ceremony transcript verification (each contribution attested and chained), and/​or eliminated by choosing transparent setups (FRI/STARK, Bulletproofs). Recorded with discharged_by = null because it is ACCEPTED with justification, not discharged by another property.

formalization.signature: Security parameter λ; advantage Adv_A(λ) of any PPT adversary A against the assumption game; CRS provenance predicate honestCeremony.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Hardness:  ∀ PPT A . Adv_A(λ) ≤ negl(λ).
Setup honesty:  honestCeremony  ≡  ∃ participant i . secretᵢ destroyed  (1-of-n honesty)  ∨  transparentSetup.
formalization.state_machine: n/a — assumption node, no transition behaviour.
formalization.type_theoretic: Serves as an axiom in the ambient logic: properties depending on it are theorems of the form `assumption ⊢ guarantee`; the assumption is an undischarged hypothesis in the assurance proof tree.

relationships.note: Holding the assumption is exactly the absence of this failure; tracked so its risk is explicit.

attack_surface.pattern: algorithmic or quantum advance breaks the assumed-hard problem
attack_surface.notes: Maintain crypto-agility and a post-quantum migration path.

attack_surface.pattern: a setup participant keeps the CRS trapdoor, enabling forged proofs
attack_surface.notes: Multi-party ceremony with public transcripts; prefer transparent setups.

attack_surface.pattern: security level chosen too low for the threat horizon
attack_surface.notes: Select parameters to a documented bit-security target.

attack_surface.pattern: a scheme proven in the ROM is instantiated with a hash that fails the needed properties
attack_surface.notes: Use well-vetted hashes; strong domain separation.

metrics: ceremony participant count and attestation chain

strategies.notes: Best-effort confidence; assumptions are believed-hard, not proven-hard.
Removes the trusted-setup assumption entirely (hardness assumption remains).

static: document the exact assumption set per security property
design_patterns: explicit assumption ledger in the assurance case

assumptions.statement: This node IS the assumption; it is accepted with documented justification rather than discharged.

provenance.notes: Canonical assumption sink: depended on by BPO:0003, BPO:0070, BPO:0073. Exemplifies a deontic ASSUMPTION-role node with null discharge — the kind of undischarged hypothesis an assurance review must surface.
